title: The signed-offer hand-over, the signature fact and the settlement instruction are not specified for rwb-treatment
source: Legacy RWB-E3-008 sections 1 to 19 (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md lines 1666 to 1765); FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v4 A2.8; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 T3.1, T3.2, T4 RESTRUCTURE and SETTLEMENT, T5.1, T5.2.1, T5.2.2 and T-A.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16 and R-SET-10; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03, DP-05, DP-13 and DP-19 and R7.2 s12
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC4; 9 State transitions; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.5; 12.7; 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: One combined row for the signed-offer routing. (1) No source publishes the shape of the thing that carries a signed offer to operations: the TSD names TreatmentWorkflow as the stage workflow that P3 calls, and the legacy story moves one case status, but no element, property set or result type is defined anywhere, and the endpoint table of the legacy story lists only the treatment create and read. (2) The signature fact has no defined route. The legacy systems column names EasyApp e-signature, TSD T5.2.2 names contract generation and e-signature as a Temporal activity of P5 rwb-document, and the FSD trigger line says 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', so no source states whether the verified signature arrives as an event, a signal or an activity answer, nor how a signature that arrives after the offer validity date is resolved against the offer timer. (3) TSD T3.1 carries signature_status (DF-TRT-030) and no signed-at, route, instruction or rule-version column, although R-RES-16 needs a verification flag and the acceptance criteria need the rule version recorded. (4) The settlement instruction that R-SET-10 raises has no owner and no operation: the legacy data table names partner_instruction, which the Ownership Map gives to S9 rwb-partner, the TSD T5.2.2 lists only postProceeds of P8 rwb-payment, and no published operation raises an instruction. (5) The operations (booking) queue of the two rules and the one-working-day timer of R-RES-16 and R-SET-10 belong to the case, which rwb-case owns, and no contract states how a stage hands a case to that queue.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E3-008 sections 1 to 19 (AC2 'Then the case moves to WITH_OPS_BOOKING', AC3 'Then route the case to operations and raise the payment instruction', Data rows partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016, Endpoints table with POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments and GET /api/recovery/v1/treatments/{treatmentId} only); FSD S2 v4 A2.8.2 ('Integration points. Workbench, the Workbench document hub, ALS and GL', step 1 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer') and A2.8.3.3 ('None; runs unattended'); TSD S2 v3 T3.1 (signature_status DF-TRT-030 only, no signed_at, route or instruction field) and T5.2.1 (TreatmentWorkflow; settlement and deed-in-lieu sagas, called by P3) and T5.2.2 (contract generation and e-signature as a P5 Temporal activity; postProceeds as a P8 Temporal activity; no instruction operation); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16 ('timers 1 working day', systems 'EasyApp e-signature, Workbench') and R-SET-10 ('Route the case to operations and raise the payment instruction', systems 'EasyApp e-signature, Workbench'); TSD S2 v3 T-A.1 (API-S2-001 to API-S2-004, none of them a signature or a hand-over path)
area: Contract: signed offer hand-over and settlement instruction
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-treatment tech lead, the P3 case-workflow owner and the P8 payment owner
proposed: Publish the SignedOfferHandover element as the result of the signed branch of TreatmentWorkflow, with the signature fact taken from the forwarded case event and recorded as signature_status, the five facts without a column recorded on the decision record, and the settlement instruction flagged on the element and raised by rwb-payment and rwb-partner; bind the route to WITH_OPS_BOOKING and WITH_OPS_SETTLEMENT as the rules state them; confirm the signature route, the instruction owner and the operations queue with the solution architect, the P5, P8 and S9 owners and the P3 case-workflow owner at the wave 2 contract freeze.

title: The published shape of the signed offer hand-over, its required set and a path for it are not specified by any source
source: Legacy RWB-E3-008 Endpoints table and sections 7, 11 and 14; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 T3.1, T3.2, T4 and T-A.1; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 T5.2.1; FSD S2 A2.8.3.1; Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence and R7.2 s12
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 7 Acceptance criteria AC1 to AC7; 11 Data; 12.1; 12.5; 12.7; 13 Solution plan
description: A gap and a boundary behind the element. No document defines a hand-over element for a signed offer: the legacy story publishes no shape, API Specification v4 and TSD T-A.1 list no signature or hand-over operation, and the TSD names TreatmentWorkflow as a workflow contract only, with no result type. The element therefore has to be published as the result of the workflow branch, with the properties and the required set as a working read, and it must add no REST path — a second path would contradict the published endpoint inventory and give the same hand-over two homes. TSD T3.1 also fixes six of the eleven properties to columns and leaves five without one, so the contract has to state where those five live, or implementers will each choose a column.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E3-008 Endpoints table (two rows, both the treatment create and read) and section 11 Data (six entities, none of them a hand-over); TSD S2 v3 T-A.1 (API-S2-001 POST /api/recovery/treatment/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments, API-S2-002 GET /treatments/{treatmentId}, API-S2-003 PATCH, API-S2-004 POST /submit, none of them a signature or a hand-over); TSD S2 v3 T5.2.1 ('TreatmentWorkflow; settlement and deed-in-lieu sagas | Temporal workflow | P3 rwb-case' with no result type); TSD S2 v3 T3.1 (DF-TRT-030 signature_status and no signed_at, to_state, instruction or rule_version field); FSD S2 v4 A2.8.3.1 (R-RES-16 and R-SET-10 only, no body)
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-treatment tech lead
proposed: Publish SignedOfferHandover with the eleven properties of the working read, six mapped to treatment fields and five recorded on the decision record, as the result of the signed branch of TreatmentWorkflow, and add no REST path and no error code; confirm the property set and the required set at the wave 2 contract freeze with the parent stage contract, the settlement instruction and the wave 2 integration harness as the pinned consumers.
